newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Shares in Driefontein rally on GFSA.
newsitem.headline: Shares in Driefontein rally on GFSA.

text.p: Shares in mining house Driefontein Consolidated Ltd livened up on Thursday after the black empowerment group New Africa Investment Ltd(Nail) said it planned to buy a stake in Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd (GFSA), dealers said.

Driefontein, which holds a 40 percent stake in Gold Fields, the world's third largest gold producer, through its shareholding in Asteroid Ltd, rose 145 cents to 42.20 rand after Nail announced its move.
"The one looking up at the moment is Driefontein because of that story with Nail and Gold Fields," one dealer said.
"All those shares involved in that takeover are rising at the moment," the dealer added.

In a cautionary notice to shareholders on Thursday Nail said it was in dicussions with Gold Fields and its Driefontein unit to acquire their shareholdings in Asteroid Ltd, which holds 40 percent of GFSA Holdings Ltd.

Nail said through its move it aimed to buy an effective 17.2 percent stake in Gold Fields which will give it joint control of the mining house with the Rembrandt Group Ltd which already owns a similar stake.
